 Agnez Mo: From Jakarta to Hollywood, on Her Own Terms
 By: 
 Pamela Price 
 Featured, Film, Music, TV 
 October 26, 2026, 
 4:00 am 
 Photo Credits: Shane Mahood/Prime 
 For more than three decades, Agnez Mo has been a force in entertainment. A household name in her native Indonesia long before setting her sights on the international stage, the singer, songwriter, dancer and actress has built a career defined by reinvention, ambition and an unwavering commitment to her craft.
 LATF USA sat down with Agnez shortly after the unveiling of her wax figure at Madame Tussauds Hollywood , a historic milestone making her the first Indonesian artist to be immortalized at a Madame Tussauds location in the United States. More than a celebration of her success, the moment represented something deeply meaningful to the global entertainer: the power of representation and the possibilities that come with breaking boundaries.
 Now, with a significant role in the fourth season of Amazon Prime Video’s Reacher and an upcoming film alongside Nicolas Cage and Michael Sheen , Agnez is stepping into another chapter of her already extraordinary career.
 But to call it a Hollywood breakthrough would overlook everything she has accomplished to get here.
 “I always feel like whenever I have more life experiences, I actually become a better artist,” Agnez told LATF.
 Her journey began at just six years old, when she released her first album in Indonesia. An academically gifted child who consistently ranked at the top of her class, Agnez remembers feeling different from her peers. By nine, she had an unusual ambition: to become a teacher who could reach people around the world through computers and the internet.
 This was long before social media, smartphones and the digital platforms that would eventually connect artists to millions of fans across continents.
 Today, she recognizes something almost prophetic about that childhood dream. Through music, entertainment and her global influence, she has found a way to inspire audiences far beyond the borders of her home country.
 Her transformation from Agnes Monica to Agnez Mo was equally organic. What began as an attempt to maintain privacy on Twitter eventually became a defining moment in her artistic evolution.
 “I’m a person first before I’m an artist, and because the person evolves, then obviously the artistry would follow,” she explained.
 It is a philosophy that has guided her through an industry constantly demanding something new.
 While audiences recognize Agnez for her powerhouse vocals, commanding stage presence and collaborations with artists including Ciara, Chris Brown, Timbaland and T.I., there is another side to her career that deserves equal attention: the businesswoman.
 With her own record label and a hands-on approach to the creative direction of her music, Agnez has long understood that artistic independence requires more than talent. From choreography and visual storytelling to the conceptual development of her music videos, she is deeply involved in shaping how her work is presented.
 That commitment to creative ownership is perhaps most evident in what she revealed about her unreleased music.
 “I do have the music ready,” she shared. “…it’s been sitting in my folder.” 
 Despite having an album prepared, she continues to write and record, refusing to release material simply to satisfy expectations.
 “I also don’t wanna just put it out for the sake of putting it out.” 
 Her music videos, she explained, are ambitious productions that require considerable preparation. She has already written elaborate storyboards for upcoming releases, but bringing those concepts to life requires the same dedication she is now investing in her acting career.
 Rather than rush the process, she is choosing to give each project the attention it deserves.
 “At this stage of my career, I wanna work on things that gets me excited.” 
 Agnez Mo in Reacher 
 For Agnez, joining the cast of Reacher marked a return to acting after approximately 15 years away from the craft. Entering an established production could have been intimidating, particularly alongside its star, Alan Ritchson . Instead, she found an environment that encouraged her to take creative risks.
 She praised Ritchson and the production team for creating a respectful atmosphere, particularly while filming physically and emotionally demanding scenes.
 Her character, Lila Hoth, offered an opportunity to explore psychological complexity rather than a conventional supporting role.
 “You’re not just playing a damsel in distress, you’re playing Lila Hoth who plays a damsel in distress,” she explained.
 The character’s shifting identity required a layered performance, while the action sequences demanded months of physical preparation. Drawing on her background in Wushu, Muay Thai and boxing, Agnez spent five months training in martial arts and fight choreography.
 And she hasn’t lost her sense of humor about the experience.
 “I actually have a mean hook,” she laughed, adding that she also has a formidable jab.
 Her next project carries an unexpected personal significance.
 Agnez is preparing to travel to London for C.L.A.Y. , a cyber thriller starring Nicolas Cage and Michael Sheen .
 While sharing a screen with two acclaimed actors would be a milestone for any performer, Cage holds a particularly special place in her artistic history.
 “Face Off was literally the one movie that inspired me to be an actor,” she revealed.
 The 1997 action thriller, in which Cage and John Travolta exchange identities, fascinated the young Agnez with its exploration of duality and morally complicated characters. She credits the film with influencing her own choices as an actress, including her interest in characters with conflicting personalities and psychological depth.
 Decades later, she finds herself preparing to work alongside the very actor who helped shape those ambitions.
 But nostalgia alone didn’t persuade her to accept the role. When she read the script for C.L.A.Y. , she immediately recognized an opportunity to explore something different from her Reacher character.
 Throughout her career, Agnez has remained connected to her Indonesian heritage, incorporating traditional dance, cultural references and musical influences into her performances. From traditional Indonesian clothing in her international single “Coke Bottle” to choreography inspired by Indonesian dance and subtle references to Jakarta in “Get Loose,” these elements have always been part of her artistic language.
 But she is careful to distinguish authentic representation from something merely performative.
 “I want my representation to be my presence,” she said. “My presence should be enough representation,” she added.
 To Agnez, cultural identity is not simply expressed through clothing, choreography or visual symbols. It is reflected in the impact an artist makes and the doors they help open for others. Her Madame Tussauds wax figure in Hollywood is one tangible reflection of that international influence, but she sees the greater achievement as inspiring others to recognize their own possibilities.
 Despite her demanding schedule, Agnez makes a conscious effort to protect her personal life. She deliberately blocks out time on her calendar for what she calls self-love, whether that means spending time with close friends, visiting neighborhood restaurants or simply enjoying ordinary moments away from the entertainment industry.
 “You’re a person first before you’re an artist,” she emphasized.
 It is a lesson learned through years of navigating an extraordinary career, and one that continues to inform her decisions. As she prepares for London, develops new music and embraces another wave of acting opportunities, Agnez isn’t interested in following a conventional timeline.
 She has already demonstrated that success can take many forms, and that reinvention doesn’t require abandoning the identity that made an artist successful in the first place.
 “I need to be shaken out of my comfort zone,” she said.
 For an artist who has spent more than 30 years building her career, perhaps that is the most revealing statement of all.
 Agnez Mo isn’t starting over. She’s still becoming.
 And she’s doing it on her own terms.
